issues.body: The server binds `0.0.0.0:3000` on the host, then the script unconditionally runs an `alpine/socat` container with `--network host` and asks it to listen on port 3000. On native Linux, host networking is the literal host network namespace, so socat cannot bind that already-occupied address. Because the `docker run -d` is under `set -e`, the run aborts before the CTH starts. This contradicts the adjacent claim that the sidecar is a harmless passthrough and is especially relevant because the workflow directs the harness to a self-hosted runner.
issues.fix_hint: Detect Docker Desktop versus native-Linux host networking and start the socat forwarder only where the VM-to-host hop is needed. On native Linux, omit the forwarder and let the host-network CTH connect directly to the host server. Add a shell-level test or preflight check covering both networking branches.
issues.title: Host-network forwarder conflicts with the server on native Linux

verdict.summary: The new harness is not portable to the self-hosted Linux runner configuration it documents: it unconditionally starts a host-network socat listener on the same host port already occupied by the server. This prevents the harness from reaching its actual test execution on native Linux.
